claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies in this guide, and following them improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`, typically from a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Pulumi's recommended rule is that a repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights how Pulumi consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
A single PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines a package, with components living alongside it.
Using a single monorepo with one giant package for all components forfeits meaningful semantic versioning; every release versions every component the same way, which violates semver.
Pulumi recommends one package per repository, grouping cohesive components in a package, and not using one giant package monorepo.
Link anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages exist on the packaging-components page.
